stem:
A patient without known diabetes has a 75 g oral glucose tolerance test at 27 weeks. The service uses the following current Australian thresholds.

| Sample | Patient result | GDM diagnostic range |
|---|---:|---:|
| Fasting | 5.4 mmol/L | 5.3–6.9 mmol/L |
| One hour | 9.9 mmol/L | At least 10.6 mmol/L |
| Two hours | 8.6 mmol/L | 9.0–11.0 mmol/L |

Which interpretation is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: The test is normal because both post-load values are below threshold
options.explanation: A normal post-load response does not cancel a diagnostic fasting value. Each time point is assessed separately.

options.label: B
options.text: The result is indeterminate until two samples exceed threshold
options.explanation: Only one value in the diagnostic range is required; two abnormal samples are not necessary.

options.label: C
options.text: The fasting result establishes overt diabetes first detected in pregnancy
options.explanation: A fasting glucose of 5.4 mmol/L lies in the supplied GDM range. The fasting threshold for overt diabetes is at least 7.0 mmol/L.

options.label: D
options.text: An HbA1c is required before gestational diabetes can be diagnosed
options.explanation: HbA1c does not replace the pregnancy OGTT at this gestation or need to confirm this diagnostic result.

options.label: E
options.text: The fasting result is sufficient to diagnose gestational diabetes
options.explanation: The fasting concentration exceeds the supplied GDM threshold. The normal one- and two-hour values do not change that classification.

context: One diagnostic value on the pregnancy OGTT is sufficient for GDM.
